about.title: Victorville Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member is heavy enough without having to decode a legal process. Victorville recorded 23 traffic deaths in 2025, and behind each number is a household that changed overnight. Reported collisions here cluster along Bear Valley Road, Amargosa Road, Mojave Drive, and Route 395, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. seeing the most activity. Under California law, a wrongful death claim is a civil action that belongs first to a spouse or domestic partner and children, then to certain dependents or heirs. It runs separately from any criminal case in San Bernardino County and generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, with a shorter window when a government entity is involved. Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the love, companionship, and guidance that no invoice can capture. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. The independent attorneys in our network work on contingency: no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My loved one died in a crash on Route 395 near Victorville. Does the criminal case have to finish first?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves on its own track, separate from any charges the San Bernardino County District Attorney may pursue. Families sometimes wait, assuming one case controls the other, and lose time against the two-year deadline. An attorney can explain how the two processes interact without you having to put your claim on hold.

items.question: What losses can our family actually recover in a California wrongful death claim?
items.answer: California recognizes both financial and personal losses. Financial losses typically include funeral and burial expenses and the income or support the person would have contributed over time. Personal losses cover the loss of love, companionship, comfort, and guidance. No amount is promised, but the law does allow families to seek both categories.

items.question: I am a sibling. Can I bring a wrongful death claim for my brother in Victorville?
items.answer: Standing in California starts with a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children. If there are none, certain dependents or heirs under the state's intestate succession rules may be able to file, which can sometimes include siblings depending on the family structure. Because this turns on specific facts, it is worth a free conversation with an independent attorney rather than guessing.
